text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: node node-gpu-17 reporting CUDA_OOM despite reported headroom on pool-redwood-3. Metric spike at 12:03 UTC, 15% request error rate increase. Auto-escalation to incidents channel.

maya: seeing repeated `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` from runtime on a handful of containers. Headroom reported at ~1.3GB across node but allocator failing to satisfy 256MB spikes.

liam: can you paste the allocator debug dump? I want reserved block counts and free slab sizes.

maya: pasted below — truncated for thread:
```
ALLOCATOR DUMP - node-gpu-17
timestamp: 2026-03-15T12:04:02Z
total_gpu_mem: 48GB
reserved_blocks: 128 (avg size 16MB)
spare_pool_free: 1.3GB
kv_cache_reserved: 6.7GB
active_allocations: 39.5GB
fragmentation_estimate: 24%
largest_contiguous_free: 120MB
pending_prefetches: 4
```

samir: largest_contiguous_free 120MB — that's the issue. Headroom number includes many small free fragments and reserved KV blocks that aren't splittable. Request tries to allocate 320MB continous buffer -> OOM.

kev: this matches the crash logs where allocator tries `cudaMalloc(335544320)` and fails, then runtime retries with fallback and container crashes.

ops-jen: customer-facing impact? any user requests 5xx?

maya: yes, roughly 7% of requests hitting that node returned 500s over last 6m. Affected model: open-llm-variant-7b, mostly long-context chat requests.

liam: immediate mitigation suggestions? We can try: 1) evict KV cache on that node, 2) force spill of some reserved blocks to sparepool, 3) soft-reserve override to allow serving smaller packed allocations, 4) cordon & drain to shift traffic.

samir: evicting KV cache likely cheapest and fastest. But note: KV cache is accounting for 6.7GB — eviction will increase latency for repeated requests but reduce OOM.

maya: starting KV cache eviction script now (`/ops/evict_kvcache --node node-gpu-17 --threshold 0.3`).

incident-bot: runbook step executed: kvcache-evict started by maya at 12:06:18Z.

maya: evict script completed, freed ~5.9GB, spare_pool_free now 6.9GB per quick telemetry.

liam: can we also reduce prefetch window for that node? Prefetches hold contiguous buffers.

maya: lowering prefetch window for node-gpu-17 to 0.2s (was 1.0s) via route override. Applied.

ops-jen: any container restarts during this?

maya: two container restarts observed at 12:05:32Z and 12:06:45Z before eviction. No restarts after eviction.

kev: telemetry shows no more `cudaErrorOutOfMemory` after 12:08 for ~4m, error rate falling back to baseline ~0.8%.

liam: still concerned about fragmentation; reserved blocks are pinned by old versions of the allocator that don't support splitting. We should identify why reserved_blocks count jumped to 128.

samir: I see a spike in dedicated-reserve churn at 11:58Z when a rollout triggered ephemeral warm pools. Those warm tasks requested small reserves and never released due to a race in reserve-release path.

maya: filing a follow-up issue: RESERVE-LEAK-3101 to track the leak and patch. Assigning to samir.

samir: taking it. I'll add a telemetry alert for reserve-churn > 50/min on a node and instrument release path.

liam: for immediate safety, suggest adding an automated soft-fallback: when largest_contiguous_free < 2x typical allocation size for a model, route traffic away from node and mark degraded. Can we add a short-term policy?

ops-jen: yeah let's do routing fallback for 10 minutes to avoid thrash while Samir fixes. Also notify affected customers.

incident-bot: oncall handoff reminder: @maya will hand to @liam at 12:30Z if still active.

maya: notifying SRE oncall and Customer Success: tagging @cs-lead to prepare messages. Affected customers: 3 mid-market tenants on region-us-west with requests served from pool-redwood-3.

ops-jen: CS draft: "We observed an incident causing intermittent 500s for certain long-context requests on select models between 12:03–12:10 UTC. Mitigation applied; full service restored. Root cause under investigation: GPU allocator fragmentation and reserved-block leakage." Approve?

cs-lead (via DM): please add that no model weights were corrupted and no data exfiltration.

maya: approved. Sending messages.

liam: postmortem action items I'll own: 1) reserve-release race fix (samir has initial), 2) allocator enhancement to support split-reserves, 3) routing policy by largest_contiguous_free, 4) add prefetch backpressure when contiguous free drops below threshold.

samir: timeline note: incident detected 12:03, mitigation applied (kvcache eviction + prefetch reduce + routing fallback) by 12:07; error rate normalized by 12:09.

kev: adding logs snippet for the failing allocation:
```
[12:05:31] runtime: trying allocate 320MB -> cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[12:05:31] allocator: free fragments total 1.3GB but largest_contiguous 110MB
[12:05:31] runtime: fallback attempt -> allocate 128MB -> success
[12:05:32] container: crash (oom) pid=12453 exit=137
```

maya: closing incident channel for now. Will reopen if errors reappear. Leave open follow-ups in RESERVE-LEAK-3101 and ALLOC-SPLIT-2987.

incident-bot: incident closed (auto) at 12:21:00Z. Severity: Sev2. Customer impact: intermittent 500s for ~7% of requests on 3 tenants for ~6 minutes. Postmortem owners: samir, liam.

maya: :thumbsup: Thanks team."
